_comment: HISTORY (long forms in git): seeded 2026-07-28 from a reader-panel FAIL; renamed 2026-08-03 when the slug mismatch was found (the old filename never loaded); fact pins moved out of notes into prohibitions 2026-08-03 because notes render under a quota header; cycles 3-11 accreted 37 prohibitions from successive panel rounds. REWRITTEN FROM SCRATCH 2026-09-03 (PR #538, register R-081..R-086, R-256..R-289; Phase A report section 2). The accreted file was inducing the errors it was meant to prevent: four pins stated facts the Autobiography contradicts (the "no resolution is reached / Board of Trade" ending, the indenture exit, the 1749 Academy date, the London-access story), six governed episodes the book does not contain, and the cross-surface rule licensed "the same specific may appear in every unit citing its anchor" — the token hammering readers flagged as the book's largest craft defect. Every pin here is chapter-scoped by its label, states the true fact AND the false variant, and carries a verbatim quote from ~/cf-canary/sources/the-autobiography-of-benjamin-franklin.txt; a claim that could not be grounded in that text was deleted, not reworded. Two claims failed grounding and are now stated as absences: "Silence Dogood" and any age for the essays appear nowhere in the Autobiography, and the 1701 Charter of Privileges is not in it either — neither may be attributed to the memoir. The three SAFETY rules are carried over verbatim (a SAFETY label is never chapter-scoped, so narrowing one is not on the table). FIX ROUND 2026-09-03 (same PR #538, review findings): the ch03 cannon pin stated a false absolute — autobio.txt:4261-4265 has the lottery paying for the battery AND its furnishing and "We bought some old cannon from Boston", with only the eighteen eighteen-pounders borrowed (4270-4275), so the Boston purchase is restored and the ban scoped to the eighteen (R-267's own three-part fix). The ch04 access pin made Collinson the escort; autobio.txt:6534 has "Mr. Hanbury called for me and took me in his carriage", so the actor is corrected. Three rules the first draft dropped are carried again because nothing else in the codebase holds them: the virtue-tracking blocker (one virtue is the week's focus, all faults still marked nightly, autobio.txt:3106-3110), the no-false-universal rule R-268/R-289 rewritten positively as a mechanism SET requirement on ch03's key takeaway and full-read opening, and the Whitefield corrector (the episode is in the source at 4078-4090 even though the last shipped package did not use it — the absent-episode criterion was retrospective). NAMED ACTOR now names the two credits Franklin himself refuses (Bond's hospital, Clifton's lamps), the fire-company duty ban is bound to the fire company so it cannot contradict the battery's nightly guard (4278-4280), the hospital pin states Bond's flagging drive as the true antecedent instead of banning it, and the university ban is scoped to the 1749 institution rather than to the word (4613-4618). ROUND 3 2026-09-03 (same PR #538): the rewrite is now accounted for rule by rule. PR #538's body carries a 37-row disposition ledger for origin/main's prohibitions (KEPT / MERGED / GENERIC with the merged PR and the contract line or gate that carries it / DELETED with the source reason) plus a 6-row ledger for its notes; nothing is dropped without a named carrier or a stated reason. Rules with NO carrier anywhere are restored book-wide rather than retired: NO RUBRIC VOCABULARY IN READER TEXT (old 36 — src/compiler/chapterBlueprint.ts:223,227 still deals the literals "transfer scenario in a fresh domain" and "verb-led action tied to the required fact" into the writer prompt, and C36 apparatusLeakage covers pipeline vocabulary, not blueprint slot vocabulary) and NO COMPARATIVE PADDING at its original absolute strength (the phrases channel renders under a quota of one at src/sections/sectionTasks.ts:301, which is a demotion, not a carrier). NO FALSE UNIVERSAL is un-scoped back to book-wide (old 29 was a book-wide panel blocker; ch03 is now an illustration in its body, where a marker does not scope). Restored from the source rather than from the last package: the indenture term (twelve to twenty-one, so about four years still to run — the old pin was true and was dropped for budget, which is not a deletion reason), the two-part Silence precept, the rebuke's conversation setting with the list's span endpoints, the Junto book-pool that failed before the subscription library, the sweeping sixpence "to be paid by each house", Granville's "the king is the Legislator of the Colonies", and the proprietary family named before any shorthand. The fire-company pin now binds the engine money to the FINES the source names and no longer says "no dues fund". Deleted on source grounds and stated as such: the 1731/1736 chronology pin (grep for 1731 hits only a memorandum heading at 3423; 1736 is never attached to the fire company, which the memoir dates only as "upward of fifty years" old). tests/franklin-scars-structure.test.ts now pins the composition so the next trim cannot be silent. ROUND 4 2026-09-03 (same PR #538): three rules are restored because their round-3 dispositions did not hold. The kite pin is back as a ch03 pin stating what the source actually does: line 6099 is Franklin's own unindented narration, not footnote 109 (which is the indented block at 6060-6066) — at 6089-6100 he reports the electrical work's celebrity and expressly declines to narrate the experiment ("I will not swell this narrative with an account of that capital experiment, nor of the infinite pleasure I receiv'd in the success of a similar one I made soon after with a kite at Philadelphia"), so the episode exists and the old rule's re-enactment and invented-peril bans are carried with it. Old prohibition 15's distinct fact ban is restored as its own ch03 pin: the almanac and newspaper were Franklin's personal profit (3533) and the memoir never makes that income a civic project's seed — NO FALSE UNIVERSAL carries only the mechanism-set requirement, not this. Old prohibition 13's notebook half is restored as its own ch02 pin (3048, 3216-3226) rather than crammed into the course pin, which is already at the word cap. CAST CONSISTENCY is new in this PR, not an origin/main rule; the PR body now says so and the structure test's docstring no longer claims otherwise.
notes: Vary sentence length and structure: a clipped run of short subject-verb declaratives is a once-per-chapter effect, never the default register, and repeated-subject strings ("Granville said... Granville stood...") merge into varied constructions.

Ground who, where and when once, early in the fast read — name Franklin, the city (Boston, Philadelphia, London) and the year — and let no example or card introduce a specific the reads never established.
Reprise a fact only to extend it: a deeper tier may restate a shallower tier's fact only by adding new detail, consequence or connection, never by reusing the same wording.

Reconstructed speech dressed as documented quotation is an over-reach: when rendering a figure's words (Granville's doctrine, the Quaker friend's rebuke, the smith's axe line), signal their status once — 'Franklin records', 'as the memoir tells it' — so dramatization never masquerades as verified quotation.
prohibitions: SAFETY (ch03): never advise beginning work on shared or public property without permission — narrate Franklin's projects as historical account, about him, past tense. The transferable mechanism is the SUBSCRIPTION: gather written commitments, then take the funded proposal to whoever owns the property. Any modern example shows permission-and-funding ON THE PAGE and BEFORE any physical work in the scene's own order — a scene opening mid-work teaches the unsafe version regardless of caveats; prefer action steps that stop at the proposal.

SAFETY (ch03): never apply the organize-and-fund-it-yourselves pattern to ARMED patrols, physical force, or safety-critical regulated functions in a modern analog. Prefer non-force analogs; if a safety-adjacent scenario is unavoidable, name legal authority, oversight, and professional standards as prerequisites on the page.

SAFETY (panel blocker, round 11): never instruct a reader to personally guarantee, underwrite, co-sign or become liable for another person's financial or practical obligation. Franklin's subscription and mutual-aid models work by POOLING many small commitments and by written terms, not by one person standing surety for another. Any action step touching money others depend on must stay inside what the reader can lose alone, and must name the written terms rather than a personal promise.

FACT PIN (ch01): arrival cash was a Dutch dollar PLUS copper — "my whole stock of cash consisted of a Dutch dollar, and about a shilling in copper". The copper paid the boatmen; the rolls cost three-penny worth. Never "he spent the dollar on rolls".

FACT PIN (ch01): the exit was covered, not criminal — "my old indenture should be return'd to me, with a full discharge on the back of it", private new indentures running on; Franklin calls seizing that "one of the first errata of my life". Never "leaving broke the law" as the whole story.

FACT PIN (ch01): the term ran twelve to twenty-one — "signed the indentures when I was yet but twelve years old", "to serve as an apprentice till I was twenty-one years of age" — so roughly four years were still to run at the break. Never nine years still owed.

FACT PIN (ch01): Bradford "did not at present want a hand, being lately suppli'd with one"; Keimer "would employ me soon". Bradford gave lodging and odd jobs only. Never "Franklin took jobs with both printers".

FACT PIN (ch01): instruction succeeded — "I made great proficiency in the business, and became a useful hand to my brother". The blows belong to the freedom disputes and keep Franklin's own qualification, "perhaps I was too saucy and provoking". Never "James beat him instead of teaching him".

FACT PIN (ch01): the essays were anonymous — "I contrived to disguise my hand, and, writing an anonymous paper, I put it in at night under the door" — and Franklin disclosed authorship himself. Never "James found him out". "Silence Dogood" and any age are absent from the Autobiography; never attribute either to it.

FACT PIN (ch02): "My list of virtues contain'd at first but twelve; but a Quaker friend having kindly informed me" he was thought proud — so Humility was added thirteenth, after that remark. Never "the system began with thirteen", and never set a thirteen-virtue scene before the addition.

FACT PIN (ch02): thirteen weeks is ONE course. The plan was to "go thro' a course compleat in thirteen weeks, and four courses in a year"; the practice thinned — "afterward only one in several years, till at length I omitted them entirely". Never state four courses a year as steady practice, and never a monthly cadence.

FACT PIN (ch02): the little book is the COURSE'S instrument — "a page for each of the virtues" — and it outlasted the practice: as the courses thinned to one in several years, "I always carried my little book with me". Never a steady notebook cadence beside a declining course.

FACT PIN (ch02): the Silence precept is two-part — "Speak not but what may benefit others or yourself; avoid trifling conversation". Every rendering keeps both halves or marks itself partial. Never the benefit-to-others-only truncation as the rule.

FACT PIN (ch02): the rebuke is about conversation — his pride "show'd itself frequently in conversation" — and the source names no other setting; never invent one ("at the table"). The list runs Temperance first, Order third ("Let all your things have their places"), Humility thirteenth; never "Temperance through Order" as the span.

FACT PIN (ch02): one virtue is the week's FOCUS, not the week's only record — "I determined to give a week's strict attention to each of the virtues successively", "leaving the other virtues to their ordinary chance, only marking every evening the faults of the day". Never "he logged only that week's virtue".

FACT PIN (ch02): the axe line is a QUOTATION — "but I think I like a speckled ax best" — and is rendered as quoted speech inside the smith's story. Never stitch it in as a noun phrase ("a speckled Ax is best won out") or as a raw research token.

FACT PIN (ch02): the Art of Virtue was never written — "my intention of writing and publishing this comment was never fulfilled" — and the Autobiography itself ends "[unfinished]". Never present either as finished work.

FACT PIN (ch03): Union Fire Company members kept "a certain number of leather buckets, with strong bags and baskets" for every fire and met monthly. Engines came from FINES: "The small fines that have been paid by members for absence at the monthly meetings". Never dues; no rotating turn of duty here — the battery's nightly guard is another episode.

FACT PIN (ch03): the sixpence sweeping subscription was "to be paid by each house" — several neighbours, never one — and it "made the people more willing to submit to a tax for that purpose"; Franklin then drew a paving bill and brought it into the Assembly. Never "not by a city-wide tax": the small win produced the tax.

FACT PIN (ch03): Bond's subscription drive came FIRST and stalled — "beginning to flag, I saw they would be insufficient without some assistance from the Assembly". Then the grant: "payment of two thousand pounds" conditional on the same sum raised privately, and "This condition carried the bill through"; donations doubled after. Never postal routes as the cause.

FACT PIN (ch03): the subscription library grew out of a POOL that failed — the Junto tried "clubbing our books to a common library" and "the collection, after about a year, was separated, and each took his books home again". Never one wealthy benefactor, and never a pool that simply kept working.

FACT PIN (ch03): the Library Company "procured fifty subscribers of forty shillings each to begin with, and ten shillings a year", and "the library was opened one day in the week for lending to the subscribers". Never "opened to the wider public"; never one wealthy patron.

FACT PIN (ch03): the Junto met Friday evenings, with queries from every member in his turn, and each member had to "once in three months produce and read an essay of his own writing". Never a weekly essay deliverable.

FACT PIN (ch03): the lottery funded the BATTERY — a "lottery to defray the expense of building a battery below the town, and furnishing it with cannon". "We bought some old cannon from Boston"; the eighteen eighteen-pounders were BORROWED — Clinton "very good-naturedly conceded eighteen". Never "a public lottery bought the cannon"; never say the eighteen were bought.

FACT PIN (ch03): 1749 is allowed as the opening year — "a house was hired, masters engag'd, and the schools opened, I think, in the same year, 1749" — the charter coming later. Never forbid the 1749 opening; never call the 1749 institution a university, though its trustees' later charter made it "the present University of Philadelphia".

FACT PIN (ch03): if Whitefield appears, he PREACHES and Franklin GIVES. Franklin "refus'd to contribute" to the Georgia Orphan House and came resolved "he should get nothing from me", then "empty'd my pocket wholly into the collector's dish, gold and all". Never Franklin organising or collecting for Whitefield.

FACT PIN (ch03): Franklin's narration reports the electrical work's fame but DECLINES the scene — "I will not swell this narrative with an account of that capital experiment" — naming the kite only in passing, "with a kite at Philadelphia". Never re-enact it as a present-day pilot; never invent experimenter-peril the memoir omits.

FACT PIN (ch03): the almanac and newspaper were Franklin's PERSONAL means — "I reap'd considerable profit from it" — never a civic project's seed money. The projects run on subscribers, fines, a lottery and an Assembly grant; never fund one from his own profits ahead of its subscribers, and never merge the two funds.

NAMED ACTOR (ch03): Franklin is the actor of these civic deeds and is NAMED as such in the fast read and the deep read; never leave the credit with unnamed friends and subscribers alone. Two credits he REFUSES stay refused: the hospital design "was originally his" (Dr. Thomas Bond), and the street-lighting idea "belongs truly to that gentleman" (John Clifton) — Franklin claims only the lamp's form.

FACT PIN (ch04): the proprietors DID meet Franklin — "they agreed to a meeting with me at Mr. T. Penn's house in Spring Garden" — and only after it "was concluded that I should give them the heads of our complaints in writing". Never "the brothers will not meet him"; never the paper delivered before any talk.

FACT PIN (ch04): Granville claimed "the king is the Legislator of the Colonies"; never reassign that phrase to an assembly or a governor. Franklin's answer keeps the crown in it — colonial laws were "to be presented indeed to the king for his royal assent". Never "it asks only for the governor's yes, not the king's word".

FACT PIN (ch04): access came by introduction, not fame — Fothergill first, then Collinson, who relayed that John Hanbury "had requested to be informed when I should arrive". HANBURY did the carrying: "Mr. Hanbury called for me and took me in his carriage to that nobleman's". Never "years of science work opened the doors".

FACT PIN (ch04): the near-wreck had no fog — "a light just before us, which had been hid by the studding-sails", the bow watchman half asleep, "It was midnight, and our captain fast asleep", the course set to pass wide of the Scilly Isles; a chance yaw saved the ship. The fog is the next morning, off Falmouth.

FACT PIN (ch04): the tax act was ALLOWED TO PASS — "when Lord Mansfield returned to the Council Chamber, where finally the law was allowed to pass", after Franklin's engagement on the assessment. Never "the Board of Trade never rules" or "no ruling ever comes"; the manuscript is unfinished, but this dispute reached that end.

NAMED ACTOR (ch04): the other side is the PROPRIETARY family — "the proprietaries, our hereditary governors" — named as the Penns before any shorthand like "that family" or "their governor"; the meeting is at "Mr. T. Penn's house in Spring Garden". Their solicitor Ferdinand John Paris acts for THEM, never as a neutral official, and the complaints are the Assembly's against them.

CAST CONSISTENCY: an invented name is ONE person — one age band, one role, one setting — across every example in a chapter, and no invented name is reused in another chapter. Never an adult in one example and a twelve-year-old in another.

NO ANALOGY GRAFTS ONTO REAL CASES: never staple a modern vignette onto a named historical case ("the same X that Franklin used"). A unit is EITHER a modern scenario judged on its own terms OR a question about the history; where it states history, who acted, who complained and who ruled must match the source.

COUNTERFACTUALS STAY COUNTERFACTUAL: never assert as a happened event what the source presents as a hypothetical or a road not taken. Franklin CHOSE sequential focus over attempting all thirteen virtues at once; no unit may narrate the unattempted alternative as a failure that occurred.

COUNT SELF-DESCRIPTION: the virtue list changes size within the narrative, so every count names its moment in the same sentence (the list as first drawn up; the list after Humility was added). A bare "the N virtues" is never acceptable, and a quiz prompt about a count names the same moment its explanation does.

NO FALSE UNIVERSAL: never present one mechanism as a chapter's or the book's single lesson when the text itself narrates others. Chapter 3 alone runs pooled subscription, an Assembly grant conditional on matching, a lottery, a legislated tax and one private man's example. A key takeaway either names the mechanism SET or scopes its claim to the projects that used one; never "every fix ran through one club".

NO RUBRIC VOCABULARY IN READER TEXT: internal rubric and blueprint slot labels — "verb-led action", "fresh-domain move", "transfer scenario in a fresh domain", promptShape and answerStyle names — are instructions to the writer and never appear in a prompt, choice, explanation or card. Every example ends on a complete sentence that finishes its own thought; no dangling comparative fragment ("Kira does the same to a stock count.").

NO COMPARATIVE PADDING: stems, card backs and explanations state their point directly. Delete any clause whose only job is re-linking the unit to the anecdote already taught ("the same X that Franklin used"). One linkage maximum per unit, and only when that linkage carries a fact the unit needs.
